subject: Post-call: Access controls & break-glass — next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@finhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: access questions from today's discovery call

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — we appreciated how the latency/cost controls looked in the console. A couple items our security/compliance team asked me to follow up on specifically around how Redwood would handle FinHealth customer data if we go into POC:

- RBAC/least-privilege: we need role granularity down to: product_readonly, product_ops, support_jit, and integration_bot. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports custom roles and attribute-based rules (e.g., region=="us" only for some roles)?
- Support access / break-glass: what is your current process for emergency engineer access? We need audit trails and time-limited access; ideally multi-party approval for any session that can access raw PII.
- Logging & retention: what logs are retained (request/response, metadata, audit events), where they live, and how long they can be retained/exported? Our compliance team expects at least 7 years for audit logs or a plan to export to our S3.
- PII handling & masking: can Redwood suppress/transform PII in logs or provide token-level masking?
- Data residency: we require US-only processing for customer data for now; what regions do you operate and can we lock the POC to a specific region?

If you can send a short checklist and any docs (RBAC patterns, break-glass playbook, logging retention options) ahead of our security deep-dive next week that would be great. Also copying Tom (security lead) to help coordinate.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Gupta
Head of Security Operations, FinHealth
attachments: FinHealth-Compliance-Questionnaire.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: access questions from today's discovery call

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Great to connect today. Thanks for the clear list — I've summarized below and attached a short RBAC patterns doc so the security team has something concrete to review (RBAC-patterns.pdf). High-level answers to your bullets and proposed next steps:

1) RBAC / custom roles
- Redwood supports custom roles and role templates; you can define roles at org, project, and route level. Attribute-based rules (e.g., region constraints) are supported via conditions on role bindings.

2) Break-glass / support access
- We offer Just-In-Time (JIT) support access with time-limited elevated sessions (default 30 minutes) and optional two-person approval. All sessions are logged and recorded in the audit trail.

3) Logging & retention
- Audit events, request metadata, and service-level metrics are retained by default 90 days. We provide log export to customer S3/GCS and a managed "long-term audit archive" add-on that meets multi-year retention requirements.

4) PII handling
- We support token-level masking, configurable prompt redaction at ingestion, and the ability to disable response logging per route. We also support field-level redaction via pre-processing hooks.

5) Data residency
- Hosted regions today: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1. POC can be restricted to us-east-1 or us-west-2 by configuration.

Next steps I propose:
- Sergio & Laura join a 60-min security deep dive with your team next Tue/Wed.
- We send you: RBAC-patterns.pdf (attached), our break-glass overview, and the default logging retention matrix.
- You send over the compliance questionnaire you referenced and any mandatory policy items.

Can you confirm availability for a technical call? If Tue/Wed works, please suggest a window and we will send calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Make inference predictable

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@finhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: access questions from today's discovery call

Hi Aisha —

Following up with more detail from the engineering side so your security team has concrete controls to validate ahead of the deep-dive. Below are patterns & options we typically propose for regulated customers (FinHealth-ish):

RBAC / least-privilege patterns
- Role model: System (platform) roles, Org roles, Project roles, Route-level roles. You can create custom roles with fine-grained permissions such as: models.infer, cache.read, cache.invalidate, logs.read, logs.export, support.jit.
- Attribute-based access: role bindings support conditions (e.g., allowed_regions: ["us-east-1"]) and attribute constraints (team=="ops").
- Service accounts: integration_bot credentials can be scoped to specific routes and time windows.

Support access & break-glass
- Default flow: support_jit request -> pagerduty (owner notification) -> optional two-person approval -> ephemeral session created via AWS STS (assume-role) with TTL.
- All break-glass actions generate an immutable audit event (who, why, duration, approvers) and store session recordings (if enabled).
- We can add a pre-approval policy so any break-glass that would access raw PII requires explicit customer approver.

Logging & retention
- Types of logs: control-plane audit events, per-request metadata (no full request/response payload by default), optional full payload logging (opt-in).
- Masking: built-in token masking + configurable regex-based scrubbing. We also provide a pre-ingestion hook so you can redact fields before anything is written to logs.
- Export options: daily export to customer S3 (encrypted w/ customer KMS key) and/or streaming to your SIEM via Kinesis/CloudWatch. Managed long-term retention available.

Data residency & encryption
- You can pin workloads to specific regions. All at-rest data is encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integration available for Private deployments).

Compliance artifacts
- We have SOC 2 Type II, and can share our attestation and security whitepaper. For some customers we also provide a scoped SOC package and role-based evidence buckets.

Attachments: brief RBAC-patterns.pdf (Marissa attached) and a small diff doc I used in previous POCs (rbac-templates.txt).

Operational note (ask): if FinHealth needs 7-year audit retention, we'll propose: 90-day default + automatic daily export to your S3 with lifecycle rules to Glacier/Archive (we'll document the export cadence in the MAP).

Happy to run the deep-dive — please pick a slot and I'll bring an engineer to talk logs/audit export specifics.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@finhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: access questions from today's discovery call

Aisha —

Quick security note from my side before the deep-dive. Two operational controls I'd like to highlight so FinHealth can validate them against your checklist: 

1) Audit retention & export
- We will enable daily export of audit events to your S3 encrypted with your KMS key. Our default internal retention is 90 days, but exports provide irrevocable custody for your archives. We'll include a sample IAM role/policy in the MAP to automate export.

2) Break-glass approval & evidence
- Break-glass requires: (a) a documented request with business justification, (b) two approvers (one Redwood, one customer) for sessions accessing raw PII, and (c) automatic notification to your security channel + email. The session token is short-lived and the action is captured in the audit event with a signed witness record.

Additional asks for the deep-dive: please share the parts of the compliance questionnaire that are "must-have" (hard blockers) vs "nice-to-have". That will let us prepare artifacts (SOC2 pages, KMS/key rotation docs, sample log export policies).

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Trust & Security, Redwood Inference
